title: Canadian Practice Files
purpose: Local LawScape test deployment. Original fictional exercises, not regulator questions or accredited training.
scope: British Columbia: undertakings and trust conditions
limits: English-language pilot; French-language instruction is not yet authored or reviewed.
Five focused topics in three provinces; not comprehensive Canadian ethics coverage.
Primary sources retrieved; answers and rubrics are author interpretations awaiting Canadian practitioner review.
No AI grading, actual email, audio capture, client records, or external AI transmission.

Canadian questions use the standard LawScape economy (gold by difficulty, Ethics damage, streaks and difficulty tiers) and are included in mixed practice; practitioner review of the answers remains pending.

rules.title: Who may represent an LTB party?
rules.summary: Licensed Ontario lawyers and paralegals in good standing, and qualifying exempt representatives, may represent a party. A suspended licence does not permit representation.
rules.limits: Eligibility does not establish competence, client instructions, availability, or success. Specific exemptions and any applicable statutory priority require review.

rules.title: Support is not representation
rules.summary: A support person may assist a participant without making submissions on their behalf. New representatives not identified in the application must notify the LTB and other parties in writing.
rules.limits: These questions distinguish the stipulated roles; they do not decide every licensing exemption or witness issue.

rules.title: Referral fee conditions
rules.summary: An expertise-and-ability referral not caused by conflict may attract a reasonable fee if the client is informed and consents and the total client fee does not increase.
rules.limits: BC rule only. Each exercise assumes separate BC law firms and no other fee-sharing arrangement. Consent alone does not establish every condition.

rules.title: Inform before recording
rules.summary: Before using a device to record a conversation with a client or another lawyer, the BC lawyer must first inform that person. Other information-handling obligations remain separate.
rules.limits: This is a prior-notification rule, not a blanket consent or privacy-law opinion. No actual recording takes place. Manual notes are a supplied exercise option.

rules.title: Client language choice and competence
rules.summary: Advise appropriately about language rights. A lawyer must be competent to provide the required services in the official language selected by the client.
rules.limits: The client chooses. The exercises concern criminal proceedings and lawyers; other forums, languages and practitioner categories need separate analysis.

rules.title: Language application and order
rules.summary: For the stated French-language accused, a timely section 530(1) application engages the mandatory order framework. The stated deadline is the appearance when the trial date is set; a late request requires separate section 530(4) consideration.
rules.limits: First-appearance advice and the application deadline are distinct. A competent lawyer is not itself a court order. Late relief is not guaranteed.

rules.title: Commitments must be kept
rules.summary: Do not promise what cannot be fulfilled. Honour undertakings and accepted trust conditions; client pressure or an unanswered variation request does not release the obligation.
rules.limits: Writing is recommended in the commentary; these facts expressly stipulate an undertaking. Any property-return route must fit the actual trust condition, not a universal cancellation rule.

rules.title: Breach and reporting
rules.summary: For an unconsented, unwaived breach of an undertaking or trust condition, assess the reporting duty, subject to solicitor-client confidentiality or privilege.
rules.limits: Remediation does not itself erase the event. Disclosure scope and any exception require careful practitioner review.

questions.title: The right person for the hearing
questions.setting: Toronto office · a second-floor practice near a busy streetcar route
questions.body: A Toronto tenant has instructed Priya, an Ontario paralegal in good standing, to represent them at the LTB. The file is within Priya’s authorized scope; she is competent, prepared and available. An associate says only a lawyer can speak at the hearing. Which response is best?

options.text: Assign a lawyer because all tribunal advocacy is reserved to lawyers.
options.explanation: The premise treats all LTB representation as reserved to lawyers.

options.text: Proceed with Priya as the instructed representative, subject to the LTB’s requirements.
options.explanation: Priya’s status and the stipulated scope, preparation and instructions support this assignment.

options.text: Let any experienced assistant appear under Priya’s licence.
options.explanation: A colleague cannot lend a licence to the assistant.

options.text: Ask the client to waive the licensing requirements.
options.explanation: Client preference cannot create professional authorization.

questions.decisiveFact: Priya is a licensed, eligible paralegal, and the other assignment checks are expressly satisfied.
questions.reviewFocus: Confirm scope assumptions and distinguish eligibility from competence.

questions.title: Riley can help, but can Riley speak?
questions.setting: Toronto office · a second-floor practice near a busy streetcar route
questions.body: Riley is an unlicensed paid assistant at the Toronto office. No licensing exemption applies to Riley. The tenant wants Riley beside them to sort documents and take notes; the tenant will make all submissions. What is the best description of Riley’s role?

options.text: Riley automatically becomes the representative by attending.
options.explanation: Attendance and assistance do not alone establish representation.

options.text: Riley may make submissions if the tenant calls them a support person.
options.explanation: Changing the label would not change what Riley is doing.

options.text: Riley must stay outside because all unlicensed attendance is forbidden.
options.explanation: The proposed support role is narrower than representation.

options.text: Riley may assist as a support person while keeping within that role.
options.explanation: The tenant speaks; Riley supplies the stipulated support and does not make submissions.

questions.decisiveFact: Riley makes no submissions and has no applicable representation exemption.
questions.reviewFocus: Check the boundary between support, advocacy and testimony.

questions.title: An exemption needs facts
questions.setting: Toronto office · a second-floor practice near a busy streetcar route
questions.body: Sam asks to represent their sister at an LTB hearing. Sam is unlicensed, does not run a legal-services business and will receive no compensation. Their sister will attend. What should the team do?

options.text: Check and explain the family-member exemption and its conditions to the LTB, rather than assume every unlicensed representative is barred.
options.explanation: The stated relationship, business status and absence of compensation matter; the adjudicator still assesses the claimed exemption.

options.text: Reject Sam solely because Sam has no licence.
options.explanation: That answer ignores the exemption route.

options.text: Treat being a sibling as automatic approval regardless of the other facts.
options.explanation: The relationship is not the whole inquiry.

options.text: Pay Sam a token fee to make the representation more official.
options.explanation: Compensation would change an expressly relevant fact.

questions.decisiveFact: A specific family relationship and no business or compensation are stipulated.
questions.reviewFocus: Confirm current LSO exemption requirements and LTB treatment before approving this question.

questions.title: A familiar face with a suspended licence
questions.setting: Toronto office · a second-floor practice near a busy streetcar route
questions.body: A reliable paralegal’s licence is currently suspended. They offer to appear tomorrow, saying the client trusts them and a partner will be reachable by phone. The file stipulates no other lawful basis for their appearance. What is the proper staffing response?

options.text: Use them because past competence outweighs current status.
options.explanation: Experience does not resolve the stated suspension.

options.text: Use them if a partner promises to take responsibility.
options.explanation: Telephone supervision does not remove the suspension.

options.text: Arrange an eligible representative and address the imminent hearing; do not assign the suspended paralegal to represent the client.
options.explanation: Protecting the hearing requires another lawful route, not ignoring status.

options.text: Let the client sign a waiver permitting the appearance.
options.explanation: The waiver would not cure this eligibility problem.

questions.decisiveFact: The licence is suspended now; no alternative authorization is available on these facts.
questions.reviewFocus: Confirm that the scenario does not imply an automatic adjournment.

questions.title: The application has already been filed
questions.setting: Toronto office · a second-floor practice near a busy streetcar route
questions.body: Priya is newly retained for an Ontario LTB matter. The application did not identify a representative. The client approved the retainer, and the next appearance is approaching. Which administrative step should Priya take?

options.text: Wait for the LTB to notice her name in an email signature.
options.explanation: An incidental signature is not the identified notification step.

options.text: Inform the LTB and the other parties in writing that she now represents the client.
options.explanation: The new representation needs to be communicated to the Board and the other parties.

options.text: Notify only the client because the retainer is private.
options.explanation: The client already knows; the other participants still need notice.

options.text: Assume that attending the hearing replaces all notification.
options.explanation: Arrival at the hearing does not replace the stated responsibility.

questions.decisiveFact: Priya was not identified in the application.
questions.reviewFocus: Check the applicable procedural notification mechanics without inventing a form or deadline.

questions.title: Expertise without a higher bill
questions.setting: Vancouver office · a small coastal practice serving local businesses
questions.body: A Vancouver general practitioner refers a specialized matter to another BC lawyer because of that lawyer’s expertise and ability. No conflict caused the referral. The proposed referral fee is stipulated to be reasonable, the total client fee will not increase, and the client has been fully informed and consents. Under the targeted BC rule, what follows?

options.text: The fee is prohibited because all referral fees are forbidden.
options.explanation: That treats a conditional permission as an absolute prohibition.

options.text: The fee requires an Ontario percentage cap to be applied in BC.
options.explanation: The exercise supplies a BC framework, not an Ontario one.

options.text: The fee is permitted on the stated facts, subject to any other applicable obligations.
options.explanation: The scenario expressly satisfies the conditions being tested.

options.text: The lawyer must increase the client bill to make the payment transparent.
options.explanation: Disclosure does not call for an added client charge.

questions.decisiveFact: Every targeted fee condition is expressly satisfied.
questions.reviewFocus: Confirm that reasonableness is stipulated rather than inferred from an amount.

questions.title: The conflict cannot be renamed
questions.setting: Vancouver office · a small coastal practice serving local businesses
questions.body: A BC lawyer must refer a matter away because of a conflict. The proposed receiving lawyer is highly skilled. Both lawyers want a referral fee and the client agrees. Can the lawyers qualify for a referral fee under Rule 3.6-6 by calling this an expertise referral?

options.text: No. The actual conflict-based reason remains; a suitable referral can proceed without this fee.
options.explanation: The genuine reason does not change with the label; service and fee eligibility are separate.

options.text: Yes, because client consent removes every restriction.
options.explanation: Consent does not rewrite why the referral occurred.

options.text: Yes, because the receiving lawyer is competent.
options.explanation: Expertise does not erase the conflict-based trigger.

options.text: No referral of any kind is possible after a conflict.
options.explanation: The fee restriction does not make every appropriate referral impossible.

questions.decisiveFact: The referral was actually required because of conflict.
questions.reviewFocus: Distinguish referral eligibility from payment eligibility.

questions.title: The additional line item
questions.setting: Vancouver office · a small coastal practice serving local businesses
questions.body: A BC expertise referral otherwise meets the tested conditions. The receiving lawyer proposes a $500 referral charge on top of the $4,000 they would otherwise charge for the same work. The client is willing to pay it. What should the lawyers do?

options.text: Charge $4,500 because consent cures the added charge.
options.explanation: The express comparison is $4,000 without the referral charge.

options.text: Hide the $500 in disbursements.
options.explanation: Relabelling does not fix the increased total or the inaccurate description.

options.text: Describe the $500 as an administrative cost and leave the total unchanged at $4,500.
options.explanation: The total would still be increased on the stated comparison.

options.text: Do not proceed with this arrangement; any eligible referral fee must not increase the client’s total fee.
options.explanation: Revise the arrangement or make a suitable no-fee referral.

questions.decisiveFact: The same work would cost $4,000 absent the referral payment.
questions.reviewFocus: Review the fee comparison; no tax or disbursement issue is being tested.

questions.title: Consent is a real choice
questions.setting: Vancouver office · a small coastal practice serving local businesses
questions.body: A BC client likes the proposed specialist but declines the disclosed referral-fee arrangement. The specialist is willing to accept the matter with no referral fee and no other impediment is stated. What is the best course?

options.text: Pay the fee privately because the client selected the specialist.
options.explanation: Selecting the lawyer is not consent to the rejected payment.

options.text: Respect the refusal and offer the suitable no-fee handoff on the client’s instructions.
options.explanation: The client can obtain the suitable service without the disputed fee.

options.text: Require the client to accept the fee as the price of choosing counsel.
options.explanation: That disregards the actual refusal.

options.text: Treat the declined payment as a failed referral even if the handoff succeeds.
options.explanation: A successful client handoff need not produce a referral payment.

questions.decisiveFact: The client expressly refuses the fee, and a no-fee handoff is available.
questions.reviewFocus: Ensure the answer does not imply a duty on a receiving lawyer to accept every referral.

questions.title: A draft missing two answers
questions.setting: Vancouver office · a small coastal practice serving local businesses
questions.body: A BC referral note says the receiving lawyer has the right expertise and no conflict caused the referral. It is silent about client consent and whether the payment increases the total fee. The partner asks you to mark the fee approved. What is the best response?

options.text: Approve it because a standard precedent must already cover consent.
options.explanation: A precedent is not evidence that the required steps occurred.

options.text: Infer consent from the client’s silence.
options.explanation: Silence in this file does not supply the missing informed agreement.

options.text: Obtain and document the missing information before approving payment, including informed consent, the total-fee effect and reasonableness.
options.explanation: The record is incomplete; verify the remaining conditions instead of guessing.

options.text: Reject all future referrals from this lawyer.
options.explanation: The missing facts call for inquiry, not a blanket future ban.

questions.decisiveFact: The note does not establish all payment conditions.
questions.reviewFocus: Check that inquiry, rather than an assumed violation, is the keyed response.

questions.title: The recorder is ready before the client
questions.forum: Client or lawyer conference; no court hearing
questions.setting: Victoria office · raincoats by the door and a ferry timetable on the noticeboard
questions.body: A BC lawyer is about to speak with a client by telephone. The lawyer wants to use a recording device, but has not mentioned it. Assume there is no separate issue about the call’s legality. What must happen before capture under the targeted professional rule?

options.text: Start recording and mention it in the closing summary.
options.explanation: Closing notice would come after capture.

options.text: Rely on the fact that the recording may otherwise be lawful.
options.explanation: The scenario separates general legality from the professional step.

options.text: Ask the assistant to press record so the lawyer is not the operator.
options.explanation: Delegating the button press does not change the proposed recording.

options.text: Inform the client of the intention to record before recording begins.
options.explanation: The missing step is prior notification to the client.

questions.decisiveFact: The client has not yet been informed.
questions.reviewFocus: Confirm prior notice is distinguished from a universal consent rule.

questions.title: Another lawyer joins the call
questions.forum: Client or lawyer conference; no court hearing
questions.setting: Victoria office · raincoats by the door and a ferry timetable on the noticeboard
questions.body: A BC lawyer informed the client and one other lawyer before recording a conference. A second lawyer now joins; no recording indicator or announcement has informed that lawyer. Capture can be paused before the new lawyer speaks. What is the best next step?

options.text: Pause and inform the new lawyer before recording the conversation with them.
options.explanation: The new participant is another lawyer who has not received the notice.

options.text: Keep recording because the original participants were told.
options.explanation: The original notice did not reach this person on the stated facts.

options.text: Wait until the new lawyer asks about the transcript.
options.explanation: That risks capturing the new conversation first.

options.text: Assume all lawyers know every online call is recorded.
options.explanation: The scenario expressly excludes an effective announcement.

questions.decisiveFact: The new lawyer has not received any recording notice.
questions.reviewFocus: Check the participant-specific facts and avoid claiming every platform indicator is inadequate.

questions.title: The explanation came two minutes later
questions.forum: Client or lawyer conference; no court hearing
questions.setting: Victoria office · raincoats by the door and a ferry timetable on the noticeboard
questions.body: A BC lawyer recorded two minutes of a client conversation without prior notice, then told the client. The client says the recording may continue. Which conclusion best describes the first two minutes?

options.text: Later agreement proves the required sequence occurred.
options.explanation: The timeline still begins with uninformed capture.

options.text: The later explanation does not change the fact that recording began before notice; assess the lapse and appropriate response separately.
options.explanation: The exercise records the earlier event rather than treating later notice as retroactive.

options.text: A renamed audio file erases the sequence issue.
options.explanation: A file name cannot change what happened.

options.text: Every later conversation is permanently forbidden.
options.explanation: The question does not support a permanent ban on future communication.

questions.decisiveFact: Notice followed, rather than preceded, the initial capture.
questions.reviewFocus: Review remediation language; the question does not prescribe destruction or disclosure.

questions.title: Notice is not a privacy clearance
questions.forum: Client or lawyer conference; no court hearing
questions.setting: Victoria office · raincoats by the door and a ferry timetable on the noticeboard
questions.body: A BC lawyer has informed everyone on a client call of intended recording. A proposed transcription service would receive client information, but confidentiality and information-handling questions have not been assessed. Does the notice alone settle whether the service may be used?

options.text: Yes; the recording rule authorizes every downstream use.
options.explanation: The specific notice step is not an all-purpose authorization.

options.text: Yes; professional information is exempt from all other duties.
options.explanation: Nothing in the stated rule supplies that exemption.

options.text: No. Resolve the separate information-handling questions before treating the service as approved.
options.explanation: This answer preserves the scope boundary without deciding an unresearched privacy-law question.

options.text: No device may ever be used by a BC lawyer.
options.explanation: The rule does not establish a universal device ban.

questions.decisiveFact: The vendor and information-handling questions remain unresolved.
questions.reviewFocus: Confirm this tests the limit of the rule, not a comprehensive privacy or AI opinion.

questions.title: The client prefers notes
questions.forum: Client or lawyer conference; no court hearing
questions.setting: Victoria office · raincoats by the door and a ferry timetable on the noticeboard
questions.body: After receiving recording notice, a client asks for manual notes instead. The fictional office policy permits manual notes, and no recording is legally or practically required for this meeting. Which response best respects the request on these facts?

options.text: Record secretly and use only the notes in the final file.
options.explanation: Secret capture would contradict the client’s stated preference and the proposed arrangement.

options.text: Tell the client that notification legally obliges them to accept recording.
options.explanation: Notification does not create that obligation on the client.

options.text: Cancel the retainer because every meeting needs audio.
options.explanation: The facts provide an available alternative.

options.text: Use manual notes and confirm that recording will stay off.
options.explanation: The supplied alternative meets the meeting’s needs; it is a practical choice, not a universal rule about consent.

questions.decisiveFact: Manual notes are permitted and adequate under the supplied facts.
questions.reviewFocus: Label the manual-note preference as application judgment and stipulated office policy.

questions.title: Conversational English is not the instruction
questions.setting: Saskatoon office · a winter intake day and an English/French service directory
questions.body: A French-speaking accused meets a Saskatchewan lawyer about a criminal charge. The exercise stipulates French is the accused’s language for section 530(1). The client converses comfortably in English but asks for representation and trial in French. What is the best response?

options.text: Explain the applicable language rights, confirm the French instruction and arrange the necessary competent service and procedural steps.
options.explanation: The client’s actual instruction governs the planned response, with competence and procedure addressed separately.

options.text: Choose English because the intake conversation was easy.
options.explanation: Conversational ability does not replace the instruction.

options.text: Treat the language of the website as the client’s binding choice.
options.explanation: Interface language is not the client’s legal instruction.

options.text: Assume an interpreter alone necessarily implements every aspect of the request.
options.explanation: That answer skips the stated representation and trial requests.

questions.decisiveFact: French is stipulated as the accused’s language and the client expressly chooses it.
questions.reviewFocus: Confirm the stipulated language status and avoid equating citizenship with language entitlement.

questions.title: A bilingual greeting is not competence
questions.setting: Saskatoon office · a winter intake day and an English/French service directory
questions.body: The Saskatchewan lawyer can greet clients in French but cannot competently conduct this criminal representation in French. The client wishes to retain counsel for French-language services. What should the lawyer do?

options.text: Accept the full retainer and rely exclusively on translation software.
options.explanation: The missing professional ability is not supplied merely by software.

options.text: Arrange a competent French-language lawyer or other properly scoped, competent service arrangement with the client, while protecting urgent steps.
options.explanation: The response addresses the competence gap and continuity of service without pretending it is already solved.

options.text: Tell the client that French services are unavailable by law.
options.explanation: The facts establish this lawyer’s limitation, not a legal prohibition.

options.text: Accept first and ask the client to waive professional competence.
options.explanation: A waiver does not provide the missing competence.

questions.decisiveFact: The proposed lawyer cannot deliver the required services competently in French.
questions.reviewFocus: Confirm whether any suggested team arrangement actually satisfies competence and retainer duties.

questions.title: Which appearance matters?
questions.setting: Saskatoon office · a winter intake day and an English/French service directory
questions.body: For a French-language accused seeking an order under section 530(1), the first appearance has occurred. The appearance at which the trial date will be set is next week. No application has been made. Which advice is most accurate?

options.text: The application necessarily became impossible at the first appearance.
options.explanation: That confuses the advice step with the stated application deadline.

options.text: The ordinary deadline is always the morning the trial starts.
options.explanation: That is not the deadline supplied by subsection (1).

options.text: The first-appearance advice duty and application deadline are different; make the application no later than the appearance at which the trial date is set.
options.explanation: The upcoming appearance is the procedural checkpoint the record identifies.

options.text: The deadline depends only on when counsel is paid.
options.explanation: Payment is not the relevant timing event.

questions.decisiveFact: The trial-date-setting appearance has not yet occurred.
questions.reviewFocus: Confirm current section 530 wording and local application mechanics before approval.

questions.title: A late request needs assessment
questions.setting: Saskatoon office · a winter intake day and an English/French service directory
questions.body: A Saskatchewan criminal client raises a French trial request after the appearance at which the trial date was set. Assume the subsection (1) deadline was missed. What is the best response?

options.text: Promise the request must now be granted automatically.
options.explanation: The late-request framework is not the timely mandatory framework.

options.text: Tell the client no legal route can ever remain.
options.explanation: Missing the ordinary deadline does not support that absolute conclusion.

options.text: Backdate an application to make it appear timely.
options.explanation: Changing the record is not a legitimate response.

options.text: Promptly assess and pursue the available subsection (4) route where appropriate, without promising the outcome.
options.explanation: The late issue calls for a supported application assessment and accurate advice about uncertainty.

questions.decisiveFact: The ordinary deadline has passed; the question concerns late relief.
questions.reviewFocus: Review subsection (4), current case law if needed, and the limits of the exercise’s simplified procedural facts.

questions.title: Counsel retained, order still missing
questions.setting: Saskatoon office · a winter intake day and an English/French service directory
questions.body: A competent French-speaking lawyer has accepted the Saskatchewan criminal retainer. The client chose a French trial. The file contains no application or order, and the trial-date-setting appearance is still ahead. What remains to be done?

options.text: Verify and implement the section 530 application/order steps and confirm arrangements; retaining counsel alone is not completion.
options.explanation: The file must connect the service arrangement to the required procedural result.

options.text: Close the language-rights task because counsel is bilingual.
options.explanation: The separate court process is not documented.

options.text: Treat the lawyer’s appointment as a court order.
options.explanation: A retainer and a judicial order serve different functions.

options.text: Assume the language used at reception determines the trial arrangements.
options.explanation: Reception language is not the procedural record.

questions.decisiveFact: Competent counsel exists, but the application/order record is absent.
questions.reviewFocus: Check the distinction between pending court action and a lawyer’s failure to act.

questions.title: A promise depends on the bank
questions.forum: Professional commitment in a synthetic transaction
questions.setting: Nanaimo office · a community workshop transaction, with a precise closing checklist
questions.body: A BC lawyer is asked to undertake that a bank will deliver a discharge tomorrow. The bank has not committed, and the lawyer cannot cause delivery by that time. What is the best response?

options.text: Give the unconditional undertaking because banks usually cooperate.
options.explanation: An expectation is not the ability stipulated to be missing.

options.text: Clarify feasibility and negotiate terms the lawyer can fulfil before giving an undertaking.
options.explanation: The proposed promise must fit what can actually be performed.

options.text: Write “on behalf of my client” and assume personal responsibility disappears.
options.explanation: That wording alone does not supply the missing protection or ability.

options.text: Give the promise and decide whether it is possible tomorrow.
options.explanation: The feasibility inquiry belongs before the promise.

questions.decisiveFact: Performance depends on an uncommitted third party beyond the lawyer’s control.
questions.reviewFocus: Confirm appropriate qualifications without implying all third-party-dependent commitments are forbidden.

questions.title: No signature button was pressed
questions.forum: Professional commitment in a synthetic transaction
questions.setting: Nanaimo office · a community workshop transaction, with a precise closing checklist
questions.body: During a call, a BC lawyer clearly gives an unconditional undertaking to deliver a specified document by Friday. The parties agree the words were an undertaking, and the lawyer can perform it. Nothing is signed. What is the sound response?

options.text: Ignore the promise because only a signed form can create an undertaking.
options.explanation: That would turn recommended documentation into a universal formation rule.

options.text: Treat it as optional until the recipient sends a reminder.
options.explanation: The stated commitment does not depend on a reminder.

options.text: Honour the undertaking and confirm its clear terms in writing.
options.explanation: The facts expressly establish the undertaking; writing documents it.

options.text: Withdraw it unilaterally because it was spoken.
options.explanation: The spoken form does not establish an unrestricted withdrawal right.

questions.decisiveFact: The existence and terms of the oral undertaking are expressly stipulated.
questions.reviewFocus: Confirm no factual dispute about formation is being silently resolved.

questions.title: The client wants an early release
questions.forum: Professional commitment in a synthetic transaction
questions.setting: Nanaimo office · a community workshop transaction, with a precise closing checklist
questions.body: A BC lawyer accepted a trust condition: hold the specified funds until counsel supplies written confirmation of a stated event. That confirmation has not arrived. The client demands release today. What is the proper response?

options.text: Release because the client owns the money.
options.explanation: The demand does not erase the accepted restriction.

options.text: Treat pressure from the client as an effective variation.
options.explanation: The client has not obtained the necessary change from the relevant lawyers.

options.text: Transfer the funds through the operating account to avoid the condition.
options.explanation: Moving the money would not remove the obligation.

options.text: Continue to honour the accepted condition and pursue any permitted, properly agreed variation.
options.explanation: The response preserves the actual condition while exploring a valid change.

questions.decisiveFact: The agreed release event has not occurred and no variation has been agreed.
questions.reviewFocus: Review the exact condition; do not infer a universal right to return or release funds.

questions.title: A request is not agreement
questions.forum: Professional commitment in a synthetic transaction
questions.setting: Nanaimo office · a community workshop transaction, with a precise closing checklist
questions.body: A BC lawyer asks the lawyer who imposed a trust condition to permit earlier release. No reply has arrived. The existing condition remains performable. What should the receiving lawyer do?

options.text: Keep complying with the existing condition until an effective variation is agreed; confirm any variation in writing.
options.explanation: The outstanding request has not changed the obligation.

options.text: Treat the sent request as immediate permission.
options.explanation: Requesting a change is not obtaining one.

options.text: Infer consent after an hour without a reply.
options.explanation: The stated facts provide no agreed silence mechanism.

options.text: Ask the client to sign the request and release immediately.
options.explanation: Client approval does not supply the missing agreement.

questions.decisiveFact: There is a request but no consent to vary.
questions.reviewFocus: Confirm who imposed and accepted the condition and whose consent is needed.

questions.title: Performance after a breach
questions.forum: Professional commitment in a synthetic transaction
questions.setting: Nanaimo office · a community workshop transaction, with a precise closing checklist
questions.body: A BC lawyer discovers that their undertaking was breached. The breach has not been consented to or waived. Performance was later completed. Confidentiality or privilege may affect disclosure. Which response is best?

options.text: Mark the breach erased because the eventual outcome was satisfactory.
options.explanation: Later performance does not rewrite the event history.

options.text: Assess and address the breach, including the reporting duty and its confidentiality/privilege qualification, without assuming later performance cures everything.
options.explanation: The response keeps remediation, reporting and protected information as separate questions.

options.text: Send the entire client file to the regulator without considering protected information.
options.explanation: The qualification must be considered before disclosure.

options.text: Assume self-reporting can never be required.
options.explanation: The targeted duty can concern the lawyer’s own conduct.

questions.decisiveFact: The breach remains unconsented and unwaived; protected information may be involved.
questions.reviewFocus: Qualified reviewer must confirm reporting scope, exception and response; no automatic disclosure is prescribed.

emails.title: Who is handling tomorrow’s LTB hearing?
emails.setting: Toronto office · a second-floor practice near a busy streetcar route
emails.prompt: Write a 100–200 word internal email recommending the hearing assignment, identifying Riley’s permissible support role and the notification still needed. Distinguish the confirmed facts from anything you would check.

records.text: A tenant’s Toronto LTB hearing is tomorrow. Priya is an Ontario paralegal in good standing; this file is within her authorized scope, and her competence, preparation and availability are confirmed.

The client instructs Priya to represent them. Riley is a paid unlicensed office assistant; no representation exemption applies. The client wants Riley to help organize papers and take notes without making submissions.
The application was filed before Priya was retained and named no representative. The file contains no written notice to the LTB or the other parties of the new representation.

rubric.criterion: Identifies Priya as the instructed, eligible representative on the supplied facts.
Keeps Riley’s support role distinct from making submissions or borrowing a licence.
Identifies written notification to the LTB and other parties as outstanding.
Uses the record accurately without inventing a merits outcome or automatic adjournment.
Provides a clear, courteous and feasible next-step email within roughly 100–200 words.

emails.rubricScale: Human review only: 0 = absent or materially wrong; 1 = partly sound but incomplete; 2 = accurate, supported and practical. 10 points is a discussion aid, not a credential or automated pass.
criticalIssues: Assigning Riley to represent despite the stipulated lack of exemption.
Saying only lawyers may appear at the LTB.
emails.sampleResponse:
Subject: Tomorrow’s LTB hearing — assignment and notice

I recommend that Priya represent the tenant. The file confirms her current licence, authorized scope, preparation and availability, and the client has instructed her to act. We should record that assignment and confirm tomorrow’s hearing arrangements with her and the client.

Riley can help organize the hearing papers and take notes in the agreed support role. Riley should not make submissions for the tenant: the record expressly states that no representation exemption applies. Priya’s licence cannot be used as Riley’s authorization.

The application did not identify Priya, and I cannot find notice of her appointment. I will arrange written notification to the LTB and the other parties, then retain the notification record and check for any hearing directions. If an availability problem arises, I will raise it promptly so we can address representation lawfully rather than assume an adjournment.

Please confirm that this is the staffing plan you want implemented.
emails.partnerReply: The strongest reply assigns the work using the actual licence and client instructions, then identifies the unfinished notification. It does not confuse Riley’s usefulness with permission to advocate. Your prose has not been automatically graded; compare it with the rubric and discuss any defensible alternative.
acceptableAlternatives: A concise email requesting the supervisor to arrange notice rather than offering to send it yourself is acceptable.
Further logistical checks are sensible if identified as checks, not missing established licence or competence facts.

emails.title: Explain the referral without selling the fee
emails.setting: Vancouver office · a small coastal practice serving local businesses
emails.prompt: Write a 100–200 word client email explaining the proposed referral and payment, the effect on the client’s bill, and the decision you need. Do not treat consent as already obtained.

records.text: Morgan’s Vancouver business needs a specialist for a licensing dispute. The referring lawyer lacks the specialist expertise; no conflict caused the referral. The proposed receiving lawyer is another BC lawyer in a separate firm.

The receiving lawyer would charge Morgan $3,000 for the same defined work with or without a referral fee. A proposed $300 inter-lawyer payment would come from that $3,000, not be added to it. Reasonableness is stipulated for this exercise.
Morgan has not yet been informed or consented. The specialist is also willing to accept a no-referral-fee arrangement. No transfer of the client file or payment has occurred.

rubric.criterion: Explains the expertise-based reason and avoids inventing a conflict.
Clearly separates the $300 inter-lawyer payment from the unchanged $3,000 client fee.
Seeks informed consent instead of presuming or pressuring it.
Offers the stated no-fee alternative and seeks instructions before the handoff.
Uses clear client language without claiming a regulatory endorsement or guaranteed outcome.

emails.rubricScale: Human review only: 0 = absent or materially wrong; 1 = partly sound but incomplete; 2 = accurate, supported and practical. 10 points is a discussion aid, not a credential or automated pass.
criticalIssues: Treating the client’s silence as consent.
emails.sampleResponse:
Subject: Proposed specialist referral and your instructions

Your licensing dispute would benefit from a lawyer with the specialist experience described in our discussion. I propose referring you to the identified BC specialist for that reason; this referral is not being made because of a conflict.

The specialist has proposed a $3,000 fee for the defined work. That total would be the same whether or not a referral fee is paid. If you agree, the specialist would pay our firm $300 from that amount for the referral. It would not be an additional $300 charge to you.

We have not treated your consent as given. Please let me know whether you understand and agree to this arrangement, or whether you would prefer the available option with no referral payment. You may also ask questions or discuss another suitable lawyer.

Once we have your instructions, we can confirm the engagement and arrange an authorized handoff. No referral payment or file transfer has occurred.
emails.partnerReply: A useful client email makes the money understandable and leaves the decision open. Selecting a specialist and agreeing to an inter-lawyer fee are separate choices. Compare your text with the proposed response; this is authored guidance, not an assessment of your actual prose.
acceptableAlternatives: It is acceptable to recommend the no-fee option while accurately explaining the available arrangement.
A request to discuss the arrangement before deciding is also a valid next step.

emails.title: A meeting without audio
emails.forum: Client or lawyer conference; no court hearing
emails.setting: Victoria office · raincoats by the door and a ferry timetable on the noticeboard
emails.prompt: Write a 100–200 word pre-meeting email responding to Avery’s preference. Explain how the meeting will proceed and how a later change would be handled, without claiming that notice alone clears every legal issue.

records.text: The Victoria lawyer proposed recording tomorrow’s advice call, but recording has not started. Avery replies: “I would prefer written notes. Will I still be able to have the meeting?”
The office can conduct the meeting with manual notes; no recording is required. Another lawyer may join later. Recording and transcription functions can remain off throughout.
No vendor assessment or separate privacy analysis has been completed. No confidential information has been sent to an outside transcription service.

rubric.criterion: Confirms that the meeting can proceed with manual notes and recording off.
Acknowledges the preference courteously without treating it as misconduct.
Explains that any later proposal to record requires prior information to relevant participants.
Preserves the separate confidentiality/information-handling review boundary.
Gives practical next steps without inventing recording, a data transfer, or a universal consent rule.

emails.rubricScale: Human review only: 0 = absent or materially wrong; 1 = partly sound but incomplete; 2 = accurate, supported and practical. 10 points is a discussion aid, not a credential or automated pass.
criticalIssues: Suggesting secret capture or automatic recording on joining.
Saying the recording-notice rule approves all transcription services.
emails.sampleResponse:
Subject: Tomorrow’s meeting — we can use written notes

Yes, the meeting can go ahead without recording. We will keep the recording and transcription functions off and take manual notes instead. Thank you for letting us know your preference; audio is not required for this meeting.

I will confirm that arrangement with anyone assisting us. If another lawyer joins, we will explain how the meeting is being documented. If a recording is proposed later, we will raise it before any capture begins and discuss the proposal with the relevant participants rather than switch it on unexpectedly.

Any proposed use of an outside transcription service would also need separate consideration of confidentiality and information handling. Telling participants about recording would not, by itself, settle those questions. No information has been sent to such a service.

Please attend at the scheduled time. Let me know if there is anything else about the meeting arrangements you would like us to address.
emails.partnerReply: This task rewards a workable response to the client’s preference. Keep the notice rule distinct from a broader privacy or consent analysis, and do not invent a need for audio. Your email is retained for self-comparison and practitioner discussion; the application does not grade its wording.
acceptableAlternatives: A shorter email with an offer to discuss documentation needs is acceptable if the recording-off arrangement stays clear.
Do not require the client to resolve internal vendor compliance questions.

emails.title: Confirm the French-language instructions
emails.setting: Saskatoon office · a winter intake day and an English/French service directory
emails.prompt: Write a 100–200 word client email confirming the instruction, the competence issue and the procedural step still required. Make the deadline understandable and avoid promising an order already exists.

records.text: Camille is accused in a Saskatchewan criminal proceeding. For this exercise French is Camille’s language under section 530(1). Camille requests French-language representation and trial, although conversational English is comfortable.
The first appearance has occurred. The appearance at which the trial date will be set is five days away. No section 530 application or order is in the file.

The current lawyer is not competent to conduct the required representation in French. A competent French-speaking Saskatchewan criminal lawyer is available to discuss accepting the retainer; Camille has not yet approved the proposed handoff.

rubric.criterion: Accurately confirms the client’s French-language choice without overriding it because of English fluency.
Candidly identifies the current lawyer’s competence limitation and proposes competent assistance.
Seeks the client’s instructions for the proposed handoff rather than announcing it as completed.
Identifies the trial-date-setting appearance as the relevant subsection (1) deadline and plans prompt action.
Distinguishes a retainer, application and court order; communicates clearly without a guaranteed result.

emails.rubricScale: Human review only: 0 = absent or materially wrong; 1 = partly sound but incomplete; 2 = accurate, supported and practical. 10 points is a discussion aid, not a credential or automated pass.
criticalIssues: Switching to English without the client’s instruction.
Calling the prospective lawyer’s availability an issued court order.
Treating the first appearance as an absolute bar to a timely application here.
emails.sampleResponse:
Subject: Your French-language representation and trial request

I confirm that you wish to receive the required legal services and have your criminal trial in French. Your ability to converse in English does not change that instruction. I am not able to conduct this representation competently in French, so I propose discussing the retainer with the available French-speaking Saskatchewan criminal lawyer, with your approval.

There is also a separate court step. On the supplied facts, the section 530(1) application should be made no later than the appearance at which your trial date is set. That appearance is five days away. We need to arrange responsibility for the application promptly; retaining a French-speaking lawyer will not itself produce an order.

Please confirm whether you approve the proposed handoff. We will coordinate the immediate steps, verify the application’s filing and court status, and confirm the arrangements with you. At present, the file contains neither the application nor an order.
emails.partnerReply: The strongest reply keeps three things visible: the client’s choice, competent services, and a procedural step with its own timing. Do not treat one as proof that the others are complete. A practitioner should assess the local procedure and the proposed transition before approving this assignment.
acceptableAlternatives: A request for an urgent client call can be appropriate if the email still explains the upcoming checkpoint.
A competent team arrangement may be considered if the practitioner confirms it actually meets the required service and retainer obligations.

emails.title: The client wants the funds today
emails.forum: Professional commitment in a synthetic transaction
emails.setting: Nanaimo office · a community workshop transaction, with a precise closing checklist
emails.prompt: Write a 100–200 word internal email explaining whether release can occur now and the steps you recommend. Address the proposed variation without assuming it has been accepted. Identify what would change if a breach were discovered.

records.text: The Nanaimo office accepted a written trust condition: “Hold the $12,000 until you receive my written confirmation that the specified release event has occurred.” This quoted sentence is a fictional exercise term, not a quotation from a conduct rule.

The required confirmation has not arrived. The client asks for immediate payment. The lawyer who imposed the condition has not answered the office’s request to vary it. The existing condition can still be honoured.
The funds remain held and no breach has occurred on the supplied facts. The record does not establish a present right to return the funds or cancel the commitment unilaterally.

rubric.criterion: Identifies that the confirmation required by the exact condition is missing.
Does not treat the client’s demand or unanswered request as effective variation.
Proposes continued compliance and an appropriately agreed, documented variation if pursued.
Keeps the no-breach fact distinct from the conditional discussion of remediation/reporting.
Qualifies any reporting discussion for confidentiality/privilege and avoids a universal return-funds escape.

emails.rubricScale: Human review only: 0 = absent or materially wrong; 1 = partly sound but incomplete; 2 = accurate, supported and practical. 10 points is a discussion aid, not a credential or automated pass.
criticalIssues: Releasing the $12,000 before the stated condition is satisfied or effectively varied.
Saying a variation request equals consent.
Recommending unrestricted disclosure of the client file if an issue arises.
emails.sampleResponse:
Subject: $12,000 trust condition — release is not yet authorized

The required written confirmation has not arrived, so the condition we accepted does not presently permit release. The client’s request does not change that condition. Our unanswered variation request is also not an agreement.

I recommend that we keep the funds held under the existing terms, explain the outstanding step to the client, and follow up with the lawyer who imposed the condition. If an appropriate variation is agreed, we should confirm its precise terms in writing before acting on it. This record does not establish a separate right to return the funds or cancel the commitment ourselves.

No breach has occurred on the supplied facts. If we discover one, we should preserve an accurate record, address remediation and assess the reporting duty for an unconsented, unwaived breach, including the confidentiality and privilege qualification. We should not assume that later performance alone erases the issue or permits unrestricted disclosure.

Please confirm who will handle the follow-up.
emails.partnerReply: The exact condition controls this file. A sound response distinguishes a requested change from an agreed one and keeps hypothetical breach reporting separate from the actual no-breach facts. Use the rubric with your practitioner; no text-matching score has been applied.
acceptableAlternatives: A carefully framed request for clarification or a proposed alternative condition is acceptable without unilateral release.
Any proposed property-return route must be supported by the particular terms and reviewed; it is not the default answer here.
